transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. I'm Dr. [Your Name]. What brings you in today?

Hi, Doctor. Well, I came in today because I just seem to worry about everything right now. It's my clients, the market, my family, money... even just overthinking whether moving to the condo was the right decision. It just feels really out of proportion to what is actually happening in my life, so I thought I should talk to someone about it.
Have you been feeling excessively anxious or worried about things most days for at least the past six months?

Yes, it's definitely been longer than six months. I'd say this has been going on for about a year and two months now. It pretty much started right after I sold my longtime house and moved into the condo.
Do you find it hard to control or stop the worrying, even when you try?

Yes, I do. Even when I tell myself, Parin, this is not urgent, it doesn't really stop. One concern just leads to another... and before I know it, I’ve spent half an hour replaying small details I meant to let go.
Have you noticed any physical symptoms like restlessness, feeling on edge, fatigue, or muscle tension when you're worrying?

Yes, definitely the muscle tension. By the end of the day, my neck and shoulders feel really tight, almost like I’ve been bracing myself for something. And sometimes I actually catch myself clenching my jaw... usually when I’m driving between listings or just sitting at my desk working. I don't really notice the other things you mentioned as much, but the physical tension is definitely there.
Have you been having trouble falling asleep or staying asleep because of your worries?

Yes, that's definitely an issue. I mean, most nights I get into bed at a reasonable hour, but... my mind just keeps circling. I'll lay there thinking about condo fees, or tomorrow’s showings, or worrying if I missed something in a contract. 

Because of all that, it takes me a really long time to finally settle down and get to sleep. And then, when I do wake up in the morning, I just feel like I never fully rested.
Have you noticed feeling down, hopeless, or losing interest in things you usually enjoy during this time?

No, I wouldn't say I feel down or hopeless. I mean, I still enjoy my work and spending time with my family. It's really just the worrying that's the problem. I don't feel depressed, just... anxious, I guess.
Since moving into the condo, have you found yourself avoiding certain situations, people, or activities because they feel overwhelming or stressful?

No, not really. I mean, I still go to work every day, I still show properties, I still talk to clients. I haven't really avoided anything or anyone. The condo itself is fine, it's just... the financial part of it that I can't stop thinking about. But it hasn't stopped me from doing what I need to do.
Have you noticed yourself feeling more irritable or on high alert lately, like you're always watching for potential problems even when there's no immediate threat?

No, I don't think so. I haven't been snapping at anyone or feeling angry. And I wouldn't say I'm on high alert, looking out for danger or anything like that. It's really just the constant worrying in my head, not so much feeling jumpy or irritable with other people.

Have you ever had sudden episodes where you feel intense fear or discomfort that comes on very quickly, like your heart racing, shortness of breath, or feeling like something terrible is going to happen right then?

No, I've never had anything like that. My heart doesn't race, and I can breathe just fine. I don't get those sudden waves of panic you're describing. It's just a steady, constant worry in the back of my mind, but never an intense attack or anything like that.
Have these worries and the way you feel been causing you significant distress or making it harder for you to function in your work, relationships, or other important areas of your life?

Well, yes, it has been making things harder, especially at work. Things that used to be pretty straightforward, like... listing negotiations or just reviewing contracts, they're taking me a lot longer now. I just keep second-guessing myself. I've even been putting off returning calls to clients because I just don't feel confident that I've checked over everything carefully enough. It's definitely getting in the way.
